101:While any card is selected, the bulk bar runs across the board's foot, beneath its columns, beside the side panel when it is open, never over it nor over the board: a row 40 pixels tall, on the theme's raised surface with a 1 pixel line in the theme's line colour along its top, the columns shortening to make room as it slides up in motion's quick motion, and lengthening again as it slides away once nothing is selected. At its left it names how many are selected, as "3 selected"; at its right, labelled buttons, never icons alone, in this order: "Move to next sprint", which moves the selected stories in the Backlog to the end of Next sprint; "Move to backlog", which moves those in Draft and in Next sprint to the end of the Backlog; "Move to draft", which moves those in the Backlog to the end of Draft; "Draft with agent", which drafts each selected story in a run of its own, all at once, as drafting with the agent says; "Change mode", which opens a mode picker above it, the one a card's pill opens, setting the mode of every selected story to the one picked, their steps keeping their own; "Duplicate", which duplicates each, every copy just beneath its original, as a card's menu does; "Delete", which deletes them all after one confirmation naming how many, as "Delete 3 stories?"; and "Clear", which empties the selection. Every move keeps the stories' order, as the selection orders them, Draft's first, top to bottom, then the Backlog's, then Next sprint's, and animates as motion says; a move button is disabled, its tooltip saying why, while none of the selection is in the list it moves from. Moved stories stay selected, duplicates are not selected, and the originals stay so. The bar has no Send and sends nothing: a story still reaches work only through the sprint, as the sprint says.
103:Right-clicking a card opens its menu at the pointer, the same menu its hover button opens, with the same items, acting on that card alone, in place of the browser's own; it closes as that menu does, Escape among the ways. The one exception is "Draft with agent": right-clicking a selected card while more than one card is selected gives it the selection, reading "Draft 3 with agent", and it drafts every selected story, as the bulk bar's button does; every other item still acts on that card alone.
117:- A story drafting with the agent: loading, "Drafting…" with its spinner in its card's property row; error, the run's failure on its card with "Details" and "Try again", leaving the card unmarked; done, its waiting proposals counted on its card, as "3 proposals", or "Nothing proposed", muted, as drafting with the agent says; done in Draft, its stories created, "Drafted", muted, in its card's property row, with the count of any proposal left waiting for failing the spec grounding after it, as "Drafted · 1 proposal", and a run that proposed nothing, or that failed, leaving it unmarked, as drafting with the agent says
123:Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent" in its card's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's title and prompt, and the drafting panel takes the open story's place in the side panel, the story's card staying highlighted while the draft is about it.
124:A draft about a story, from "Ask agent" or "Draft with agent", never changes the story it drafts: every piece it proposes is a new story of its own, its target "New story", and the drafted story keeps its title, prompt, mode, steps, attachments, and spec citations, and stays in its column. What was the story's rewrite comes first, the first piece, a new story with the proposed title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, carrying the proposed Spec follow-up step, where it needs one, as its own step. Where a story holds more than one piece of work, the draft splits it: each other piece is a new story too, after the first, with its own title, prompt, mode, spec citations, and follow-up step, grounded as the spec grounding says. A story that is one piece of work gets only that first new story. A draft about a story proposes nothing that rewrites the story or adds to it, none of its proposals targeting the story drafted, and a follow-up step is always part of the new story it follows, never a proposal of its own.
125:A draft favours several stories over one story of many steps. Each story it proposes is one piece of work a single chain does: as a rule a Chain story, its prompt changing the spec and then the code to match it, with at most one step, a Spec step following the chain up, where the spec needs settling once the code is done. Work that would need more than that is split into stories of their own, each a "New story" proposal, never strung onto one story as further steps. Another mode, Code, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, is proposed only for a story that is only that, as a question or a change to the code alone. A story drafted that already has steps keeps them, since the draft never changes it; each new story proposed carries no more than the one Spec follow-up, and what further steps would have done is proposed as new stories of its own.
130:Several stories can be drafted at once, each in a run of its own. "Draft with agent" is an item of the menu of every card in Draft, the Backlog, and Next sprint, the menu its hover button opens and right-clicking opens at the pointer, as the parts say, and a button of the bulk bar, drafting every selected story; a card in Current sprint or Done, and a finding, has no such item. It is meant mainly for Draft's rough stories, but drafts any story it is offered on.
131:Each story drafts as "Ask agent" drafts an open story, with no request box and nothing to type: the run is told the story's title, its prompt, its mode, and its steps, and asked to turn it into a full story, a fuller prompt, the mode that fits it, its Spec follow-up step where it needs one, and its spec citations, shaped as drafting says, grounded as the spec grounding says, proposed as a new story, never as a change to the story drafted; and, where the story holds more than one piece of work, to split it, as drafting says, that full story first, the first piece, with its follow-up step, then a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with its own title, prompt, mode, spec citations, and follow-up step, grounded the same way. A story that is one piece of work gets only the first new story. The story drafted is left as it was, as drafting says. Each run is its own, in a run of its own with no session, a Question run as the proposals say, with the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts). All the runs start at once, none waiting on another, however many stories are drafted; one ending, failing, or being stopped never touches the others. A story already drafting is skipped, so drafting it again starts no second run.
132:The drafts never take over the side panel, which holds only one thing at a time, as the layout says: a story drafting this way shows its run on its own card, and opening the story while it drafts shows the story in the panel as ever, its run going on. While its run goes, the card's property row shows the loading state, as the states say, "Drafting…" with its spinner, in place of its status, and its menu has "Stop", which stops that run alone and keeps whatever it had proposed by then, in place of "Draft with agent". A run that fails shows its error on that card, beneath its property row, as the states say, in the theme's error colour with "Details" collapsed and "Try again", which drafts the story again; the error stays until the story is drafted again or opened. A run cut off when the application quits, as every run is, shows the same error once it is open again.
135:A story in Draft, drafted with "Draft with agent", has nothing to accept, since as soon as its run ends, each story it proposed is created, as accepting it would create it. That is the first piece, with its Spec follow-up step as its own step, then each other piece, in the order the run gave them, each added at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", with its title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, as the proposal cards say. A run stopped with "Stop" ends the same way, creating what it had proposed by then. Whether a story is in Draft is read when its run ends, so a story moved out of Draft while it drafts waits to be accepted, as below, and one moved into Draft has its stories created. A proposal that fails the checks of the spec grounding, one with no spec cited and no "No match", is not created, and stays on the card as a waiting proposal, as below, its card in the theme's warning colour with "Draft again", as the spec grounding says. The story drafted stays in Draft, unchanged, and, once at least one story was created from its run, is marked "Drafted" in its property row, muted, where "3 proposals" shows for a story whose proposals wait, its tooltip saying how many stories were added to the Backlog; the count of any proposals left waiting follows it, as "Drafted · 1 proposal". The mark is saved with the story, in its file, so it comes back after a reload or a restart, and is kept wherever the story is later moved. A run that proposed nothing, or none that passed the checks, or that failed, marks nothing, showing "Nothing proposed" or its error as the states say, and a mark from an earlier draft stays as it was. Drafting a story marked "Drafted" again drafts it as before, its card showing "Drafting…" while the run goes, and the stories it proposes are created after the ones before.
136:Every other draft still waits to be accepted: a story drafted in the Backlog or Next sprint, and any draft started with "Ask agent", Draft's stories included, as drafting says, shows its proposals and creates nothing until each is accepted.
137:Nothing else reaches the plan until it is accepted, as the proposals say. ## Spec Grounding

A drafted story is grounded in the project's spec, never written from the request alone. Before proposing, the drafter searches the spec for what each story touches: the requirements and behaviours it changes or relies on, the names it uses, as a feature, a component, or a property, and the sections they are in. It reads the spec as every run does, from its compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never from the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and the planning prompt of the [BakedSystemPrompts](../harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.md#baked-system-prompts) tells it to.
Each proposal cites what it found, specifically: its `suspense-story` block holds a `spec` list, one entry per element, each a link to the element in the spec's Piton source, under the spec location, never to the compiled reference: the .pi file, relative to the project directory, then `#` and the element it names, an anchor or a property on one, in the form `piton slice` takes, as `spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint`, with a short line of what in it the story touches. The story's prompt names those elements and links to them in the same form. Only elements the drafter found are cited, and where they point is the only thing that is Piton source: the drafter still learns what the spec says only from the compiled reference or from what `piton slice` prints, never by reading the Piton source, as the [ModeSystemPrompts](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts) says, and works out each element's source from what `piton slice` prints for it, which names the file each declaration is in.
The application checks each link against the Piton source when the proposal arrives: the file has to exist under the spec location, and has to define the named element, the anchor declared in it and, for a property, that property on it, as `piton slice` would find it. A link that fails either check is dropped, with a muted note on the card saying which link it dropped and why, "no such file" or "the file doesn't define Planning.sprint". Each citation, on the proposal card and in an accepted story's "Spec" list, opens that place in the Piton source, the file in the editor at the element's declaration, as the [OpenFile](../open-file/index.md#open-file) opens a file.
Where no spec element matches part of a story, as a request for something the spec doesn't describe yet, the story says so instead of inventing one: its `spec` list holds an entry reading "No match", with what was looked for, and its prompt says plainly that the spec has nothing on it yet, so the change is new. A proposal with no element at all, and no "No match", isn't shown as a story: its card says the drafter cited no spec, in the theme's warning colour, with "Draft again", which runs the draft for that story once more.
The citations are shown on the proposal's card, beneath its prompt, as a short list, each element's name, as `Planning.sprint`, and its file, muted, as a link that opens that place in the Piton source, a "No match" entry muted with a small marker, and are kept with the story once it is accepted, listed in the open story beneath its steps as "Spec", and shown in its card's tooltip. They can be edited with the story, removed, or added to by hand: "Add citation" opens a picker of the spec's elements, its anchors and their properties, found from the Piton source and searched by name, never from the compiled reference, and adds the one picked in the same form, checked as a proposal's are.
Each citation says what kind of element it is, "Requirement", "Behaviour", "Name", or "Section", shown as a small muted label before it, and quotes the few words of the spec it rests on, so what the story relies on can be checked at a glance. Grounding holds for every proposal, however it came: from Draft stories, from research that ends with proposals, and from an Ask answer's `suspense-story` block, each checked and flagged the same way when it arrives.

content.text:
Running "Draft with agent" on a card in Draft now creates the stories it proposes as soon as its run ends, or when you press "Stop", with nothing to accept. All the changes are in `src/planning.rs`.

I couldn't build or test in the project directory: the prompt files under `.suspense/system-prompts` can't be read, even outside the sandbox. So I checked a copy of the crate built with empty placeholders for those files. It compiles with no new warnings. My drafting tests pass, including the one I updated, `stories_draft_with_the_agent_each_on_their_own`. Six other planning tests fail in that copy, in drag-gap maths, spec-element search and the drafting panel's request text. My change doesn't touch any of those. I couldn't confirm the six fail without my change either, because `planning.rs` isn't committed, so there's no earlier version to run them against.

- **New stories:** each passing proposal is added at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", in the run's order, the first piece carrying its Spec follow-up step. This uses the same code as accepting a proposal, which I moved into a shared helper (`add_proposed`).
- **Failing proposals:** a proposal with no spec cited and no "No match" isn't created. It waits on the card as before, with "Draft again".
- **When it applies:** whether the card is in Draft is checked when the run ends. Backlog and Next sprint cards and "Ask agent" drafts still wait to be accepted.
- **"Drafted" mark:** the Draft card is marked "Drafted", muted, in its property row once at least one story was created. Proposals still waiting follow it, as "Drafted · 1 proposal". The tooltip says how many stories were added to the Backlog.
- **Saving the mark:** it's saved as a `drafted: N` line in the story's own `.pi` file, so it survives reloads and moves. It isn't copied when the story is duplicated.
- **Unmarked runs:** a failed or empty run adds no mark, and a mark from an earlier draft stays.
- **Drafting again:** a "Drafted" card drafts again as before, and the new stories go after the earlier ones.

I added tests for the Draft-card split, a run with one grounded and one ungrounded proposal, a failed run, and drafting a card again. The spec and the prompt didn't disagree anywhere.
